$comment: Sidecar for 2026-08-29-contact-patch-pressure-map.png. Disclosure fields are POPULATED, never defaulted - this asset is model-generated and the constraints below govern how it may be captioned.

asset.aspectRatioNote: NOT exactly 9:16. 1536/2752 = 0.5581; 9:16 = 0.5625. Close enough to read as vertical, but reelPromotability.ts compares aspectRatio to the literal string '9:16', so this asset must be reframed or the field set honestly - do not label it 9:16 to make a check pass.

disclosure.note: Any post using this asset MUST set Meta's is_ai_generated=true on the container (shared/reelDisclosure.ts). Caption text alone does not satisfy Meta - verified against their ig-user/media reference 2026-08-28.

mustNotClaim: that the heat map represents a real measurement, test, or instrument reading
that it depicts a specific customer's tire, vehicle, or repair
that it is a before/after comparison of two inflation states
any numeric pressure, temperature, or wear figure derived from the colours
usageConstraints.splitCompositionWarning: READ THIS BEFORE CAPTIONING. The image is a two-tone split - cyan left half, orange right half, divided by a dash-dot centreline. That styling strongly invites an 'under-inflated vs over-inflated' or 'good vs bad' caption. It does not support one: both halves show essentially the SAME contact-patch pressure distribution, differently coloured. Captioning it as an A/B comparison would fabricate a distinction the image does not depict. Confirmed by looking at the rendered image, not by reading the generation prompt.
usageConstraints.safeFraming: Use it as a metaphor for how tire pressure concentrates load across the contact patch, and how that shapes where a tire wears. Describe the mechanism, never a measurement.

packAssignment.whyNot: pulling is an alignment and camber problem. This is a contact-patch load-distribution explainer and does not illustrate pull. The generation prompt was aimed at the wrong pack; filing it there anyway would make it a mislabelled surface.
packAssignment.whySuggested: that pack is WEARSHAPE - 'Your tire wear has a shape'. Contact-patch load distribution is the MECHANISM that produces wear shape, so the asset illustrates that pack's causal claim directly. Second choice is 2026-08-17-summer-heat-tire-pressure, which is weaker: that pack is about TPMS and heat, and the contact patch is not its subject.

provenance.ledgerProof: balance 1934.62 before, 1932.62 after, delta exactly 2, matching the get_cost quote. Run with use_unlim:false to force the credit path so a zero delta could not be mistaken for a free-trial consumption.
provenance.originalUrlIsNotStorage: Higgsfield retains outputs for AT LEAST seven days, which is a retention floor and not a guarantee. The CloudFront URL is therefore not durable storage; this committed copy is the durable one. reelPipeline.ts:640-646 makes the same point about generation output - only Higgsfield returns its own CDN URL, and every other provider must be re-hosted through storagePut.
